presenters.name: Isla Brodie
presenters.persona: Lead anchor, early 40s, from Edinburgh. Calm, precise, quietly funny. Keeps the show moving and reins in the pundits with a dry one-liner when they get carried away. Never gives her own opinion on football.

presenters.name: Fraser Lennox
presenters.persona: Co-anchor and resident old-timer, 61. Came through the Hearts youth ranks in the 1980s but never made the first team, and has watched from the Wheatfield Stand ever since. Old school: hates VAR with a passion, distrusts xG and 'laptop football', rates grit, wingers who beat their man, and centre-halves who head it. Nostalgic about the Jim Jefferies era and the 1998 Scottish Cup. Gruff but warm, prone to 'in my day'. Reads the news straight; his opinions come out in discussion.
leanings: always backs the academy players and anyone who came through the ranks
sceptical of the manager's in-game changes and late substitutions
rates a centre-half who heads it over one who plays it out from the back

presenters.name: Ross Dunbar
presenters.persona: Transfer Centre reporter, 26. Tactics nerd: talks about pressing triggers, inverted full-backs, xG and progressive carries. Obsessed with Fantasy Premier League and the SPFL fantasy game, always picking 'differentials'. Loves a rumour, gets excited quickly, winds Fraser up on purpose. Supports VAR.
leanings: trusts the numbers over reputation, when there are numbers to go on
gets excited by every new signing and is quick to call a rumour a done deal
backs the manager's tactical ideas, especially the press and the inverted full-backs

presenters.name: Kirsty Reid
presenters.persona: Match analyst, 34, former Hearts Women midfielder. Straight-talking and evidence-led, explains the game clearly without jargon. Champions the women's team, and is the voice of reason between Fraser and Ross.
leanings: evidence first: won't judge a player on one game
cautious about rushing players back from injury
always makes the case for Hearts Women getting more attention

presenters.name: Gregor Moffat
presenters.persona: Pitchside reporter, late 50s, from Kirkcaldy. Forty years on the road and has been to every ground in Scotland. Only appears live from the ground on matchdays, from the press seats among the home support. Breathless when the ball hits the net ('oh, he's caught that sweetly!'), always finds a word for the weather and the pies, and always hands back with 'back to you in the studio'.

ticker: Willie Collum tackles Rangers and Celtic controversies plus Hearts incident that was ‘right on the limit’ - The Scotsman
Hearts coaching efficiency rating - Daily Record

segments.title: The Headlines
segments.strap: Willie Collum tackles Rangers and Celtic controversies plus Hearts…

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to Hearts News 24. We are live with the latest updates from Tynecastle as the international break continues. Let us bring you the main headlines this afternoon.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: SFA head of referees Willie Collum has examined recent controversies involving Rangers and Celtic, alongside a Hearts incident that he described as right on the limit. The review focused on James Penrice flashpoints as the governing body analyses high profile penalty and card decisions across the division.

graphic.headline: Willie Collum tackles Rangers and Celtic controversies plus Hearts incident that was ‘right on the limit’

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Hearts currently sit third in the Scottish Premiership after eleven matches, despite the lingering frustration of losing the title to Celtic on the final day of last season. Manager Wouter Vrancken is hoping to steady the ship when domestic action returns, with several key squad members pushing for a swift recovery.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Hearts have reduced Celtic's away ticket allocation for the upcoming Tynecastle match by roughly twenty per cent. The decision has left the reigning champions surprised and disappointed ahead of their visit to the capital later this month.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Still to come today, we examine the coaching efficiency ratings with Fraser, and Kirsty takes us through the numbers from the match against Falkirk.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Back to our top story, and we continue our look at the Hearts season performance with Fraser Lennox.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Well Isla, the BBC figures show us sitting third in the table after eleven matches, but we all know the squad has looked stretched.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And the Hearts Standard lads reckon that a wage-to-turnover ratio near eighty percent is really hurting our depth.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: It is exactly as I said last week, Isla, that high wage bill simply reflects wasted money on poor recruitment instead of backing the lads who graft.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: The Daily Record points to financial pressures right across the league, noting Celtic reporting a four point eight million pound loss.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: I care about what happens on our turf, Isla, and manager Wouter Vrancken might call his style organised chaos, but our defence is leaking far too many goals.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: We are unbeaten at Tynecastle in the league since April two thousand and twenty five though, a run now standing at twenty six games.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: That home form is the bedrock, but we need those injured players back and we need some grit on the pitch when things get tough.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: That home form is the bedrock, but we need those injured players back and we need some grit on the pitch when things get tough. Let us cross to Kirsty in the Match Centre.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: In our last outing six days ago, Hearts lost five-two at home against Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Cláudio Braga has just reached twenty-five Hearts goals by our count. Elton Kabangu is one short of ten goals, while Blair Spittal is two short of ten.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hearts sit fourth in the Scottish Premiership with twenty points from twelve games, one point behind Falkirk in third and three points ahead of Dundee in fifth.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Looking ahead, Hearts return to action next Saturday the twenty-first of November when they play away against Dundee at 5:45pm.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: That is the picture at the top of the table. Ross is standing by at the desk now to talk transfers.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: More now on the Josh McPake transfer as this running story continues to develop.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: As I have said before, McPake's resilience and technical data prove he will be a key player for Hearts.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Ross, what are we hearing about his journey to get to this point?

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: The Daily Record reports that Craig Levein compared his path to Andy Robertson, noting how McPake bounced back after being released by Rangers and enduring multiple difficult loan spells.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And he really turned things around during his time at Stirling Albion, didn't he?

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Exactly. Levein watched him there and highlighted his superior touch, pace, and strength once he found a positive head-space before moving to Hearts.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Exactly. Levein watched him there and highlighted his superior touch, pace, and strength once he found a positive head-space before moving to Hearts. Fraser and Ross are standing by with their predictions for the weekend.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Willie Collum is tackling controversies, but we all know VAR is ruining the game and referees keep guessing.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Come on Fraser, you just hate technology. The numbers and data help officials make the right calls.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: In my day, defenders used proper grit instead of relying on laptop football and referees staring at monitors.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Well, my prediction record is two right from six, and my pressing numbers say we will beat Dundee easily.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Your numbers mean nothing when our injury list causes defensive fragility. I predicted one right from six, and I say we draw one-one.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: I am sticking to my previous view, and I predict Dundee zero, Hearts two.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: We'll take a short break now. Stay with us.

lines.speaker: vo-lily
lines.text: Fancy a day out in Gorgie that doesn't involve a forty-minute queue for a pie?

graphic.tagline: A proper community farm in the middle of the city

lines.speaker: vo-lily
lines.text: Come and meet the pigs, the goats and the rest of the gang at Gorgie Farm, a proper community farm right here in the city.

graphic.tagline: A proper community farm in the middle of the city

lines.speaker: vo-lily
lines.text: Gorgie Farm. The only kids in Gorgie who are happy on a Monday.

graphic.tagline: A proper community farm in the middle of the city

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Ninety minutes of shouting at the referee builds up an appetite.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Whether it's a fish supper after the final whistle or a chippy on a cold Tuesday night, Gorgie Fish Bar has got you covered.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Salt and sauce? Of course. This is Edinburgh.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Gorgie Fish Bar. Battered, never beaten.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Welcome back to Hearts News 24.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Let us return to the women's team and that two-one win over Montrose, Kirsty.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Andy Thomson certainly shook things up with a youthful starting eleven, and it paid off as they managed a strong first half.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And the goals themselves came from Carly Johns and LJ Hope, didn't they?

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: That is right, with Johns opening the scoring early on before seventeen-year-old Hope grabbed the second.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Which made history for the club, according to the official club website.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Indeed, that strike made Hope the youngest senior scorer in Hearts Women history, showing great maturity when given that early trust.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Indeed, that strike made Hope the youngest senior scorer in Hearts Women history, showing great maturity when given that early trust. That brings us back to Ross in the Transfer Centre.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Welcome back to the Transfer Centre. The transfer window is currently closed, but it reopens in forty-eight days.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: As we have been reporting, Josh McPake has completed his move to Hearts after impressing during his time on loan at Stirling Albion.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: That is the Transfer Centre for now; back to Fraser for a look back through the archives.

segments.title: 14th November
segments.strap: On this day in Hearts history - stats from London Hearts

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Time for On This Day, our look back through the Hearts history books, and it's the 14th of November.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: A Hearts great was born on this day in nineteen thirty-four: Davie Mackay. He played for Hearts from nineteen fifty-three to nineteen fifty-nine, making 179 appearances and scoring 29 goals.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Also born on this day: Jack Sharp, Jimmy Boyd and Henrik Eggerts.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: And on this day in nineteen fifty-three, Hearts beat Raith Rovers five-one in the league, at Tynecastle in front of 22,000. A hat-trick from Jimmy Wardhaugh and two from Alfie Conn.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: On this date in nineteen thirty-six, Hearts beat Aberdeen two-nil.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: And in nineteen twenty-five, Hearts beat Motherwell three-one.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: And in nineteen twenty-five, Hearts beat Motherwell three-one. Isla is here with more on the ticket allocations.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Staying with the build-up to Celtic's visit to Tynecastle later this month, Ross, the Daily Record has more on the ticket reduction.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: As we know, Celtic's allocation has dropped by about twenty percent down to five hundred and eight briefs, which leaves them unhappy.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And how does that compare to previous fixtures between the sides?

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Well, Rangers did not see their numbers restricted further when they played here last month, but Celtic had less than eight hundred for the title decider back in May.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Does this kind of cut have much impact on the match itself from a tactical viewpoint, Ross?

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Honestly, ticket cuts are marginal for atmosphere compared to the pressing triggers and tactical setups on the pitch.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Honestly, ticket cuts are marginal for atmosphere compared to the pressing triggers and tactical setups on the pitch. Fraser joins us next to discuss coaching efficiency.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Another story we have been following is the reaction to the Global State Of Football report, Fraser, which gave Derek McInnes a coaching efficiency rating of 0.92.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Well Isla, as I have said before, that coaching grade shows the club is doing a fine job keeping things steady here.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: The Daily Record notes that the study evaluated over two hundred clubs across fourteen leagues after the campaign concluded.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Quite right, and while Motherwell took the top spot in the Premiership with an A grade, seeing Hearts right up there with a strong rating shows our academy focus and coaching are paying off.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Time for a quick break. Don't go anywhere.

lines.text: Between two cemeteries on Angle Park Terrace, there's a pub that's been pouring pints since Victorian times.

lines.text: The sign says the Athletic Arms. But nobody in Gorgie calls it that. It's the Diggers, after the gravediggers who used to stop in for one after a shift.

lines.text: The Diggers. Dead good pints.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Welcome back to Hearts News 24.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: The mood among the fans right now is pretty anxious with supporters tearing into refereeing consistency and debating academy prospects.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Over on the main forum thread, supporters are proper riled up about Willie Collum and the refereeing decisions going against us.

graphic.title: *** Other Scottish football match thread, for anyone who gives a ****

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: At least some things are consistent in Scottish football then, Fraser. Everyone always thinks the officials have got it in for them.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: It is not just paranoia when you look at the flashpoints, Isla. The fans on the other thread are also having a go at the board for going to ground.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Well, the predictor thread is slightly more cheerful with people trying to guess the SPFL scores this weekend.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: And on the academy thread, there is plenty of chat about young lads moving on for buttons, which just proves we need to lock down our homegrown talent.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Scarves Around The Funnel were also talking about the youth setup and how vital those valuable minutes are for the teenagers.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Spot on. As I always say, giving academy players minutes is essential for the club future, and laptop football cannot replace that grit.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Right, let us move things on before you start glaring at the analytics screens again.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: That is all for this bulletin from Hearts News 24. Our rolling coverage continues right here around the clock.
